tasks.short: Build cooperative relationships with community, consumer, employee and public interest groups.

steps.what: Review contact history and current concerns before approaching a group.

loop.input: Authorised contact records, meeting notes and concern log entries.
loop.output: Stakeholder brief with dated concerns, commitments and source references.
loop.check: Require source references; distinguish recorded statements from interpretations; specialist checks sensitive context.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per brief; missing or conflicting records go to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Dates and contacts are structured, but concerns and relationship history are recorded in free text.

steps.what: Exchange availability and arrange a meeting.
Listen to concerns, explain positions and explore common ground.
Write up concerns, proposed commitments and responsible colleagues.

loop.input: Specialist's meeting notes and existing contact record.
loop.output: Proposed record changes and commitments with owners, dates and unresolved fields.
loop.check: Compare changes with notes; never infer agreement, an owner or a deadline; specialist approves changes.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unresolved fields remain blank and enter an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes describe concerns and tentative commitments without consistent fields.

steps.what: Approve proposed commitments requiring resources or a change in position.
Send agreed follow-up and set reminders for promised actions.

tasks.design: Configure contact history, commitment fields and reminders in the {CRM}, linked to the {CALENDAR} and {EMAIL}. Bounded extraction prepares source-linked briefs and proposed record changes from authorised notes in the {DOCS}; people conduct conversations, approve commitments and review external follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact records could already hold dates and reminders, but scattered notes made useful preparation and accurate follow-up expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Small text-extraction loops can sit inside existing record workflows; AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting fields and templates.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, conflicting interests and informal promises need human interpretation. Sensitive relationship notes need careful access and retention.
tasks.human_edge: Earn trust, notice hesitation and negotiate commitments the organisation can honour.

ambition.what: Regular listening appointments for local community groups without an existing contact.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time reconstructing history and chasing actions, leaving more time for listening. Decision rights remain within the existing relationship and commitment mandate.

reach.learn: Accessible invitations, venue requirements and participation formats.

evidence.claim: Contact records, scheduling links, templates and reminders can support relationship administration; relationship quality remains human work.
Extracting tentative commitments from notes needs source checks and human review; this design has no demonstrated relationship outcome.

assumptions: The task covers a typical mix of relationship maintenance and meetings in a company with 200 to 2,000 staff.
The conversation-heavy prior is retained; administrative work is a minority of total time.
Scheduling automation starts only after the specialist chooses the contact and meeting purpose.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for a limited pilot; consultation waiting time may extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Where contact history is stored and whether it can be accessed through supported interfaces.
Whether existing notes include sensitive personal data.
Which community groups currently lack regular contact.
research_questions: How often do notes contain ambiguous commitments that cannot be extracted reliably?
Can existing contact and scheduling features cover the pilot without custom code?
new_work: Review extracted concerns and proposed commitments.
Resolve missing owners, dates and conflicting records.
Maintain contact permissions, retention rules and follow-up templates.

tasks.short: Discuss stakeholder concerns with managers and advise on business decisions.

steps.what: Gather coverage, stakeholder concerns and relevant business updates.
Prepare a briefing on emerging themes, uncertainties and decisions needing discussion.

loop.input: Dated evidence bundle and previous decision log.
loop.output: Source-linked themes, conflicting accounts and questions for managers.
loop.check: Validate references and dates; show source counts without claiming representativeness; specialist checks framing.
loop.stop: One classification and one correction pass per brief; disputed themes remain flagged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Stakeholders express similar concerns in different language, and their context matters.

steps.what: Discuss concerns, business constraints and likely public reactions with managers.
Recommend a response and explain reputational trade-offs.
Confirm the business decision and record its owner and review date.

tasks.design: A scheduled job assembles authorised coverage and concern records from the {SOCIAL}, {CRM} and {DOCS}. A bounded classification loop prepares a cited briefing; managers and the specialist discuss its implications, then a configured {PROJECT} workflow records the manager's decision and review date.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was fragmented, and interpreting concerns required manual reading. Existing reporting did not resolve disagreement about business implications.
tasks.enabler_now: Supported exports and inexpensive integration code can assemble evidence; bounded text classification can prepare themes for review.
tasks.still_hard: Coverage is a biased sample of opinion. Advising managers still requires business context, judgement and the confidence to challenge a proposed decision.
tasks.human_edge: Connect public concerns to business choices and challenge assumptions in a difficult management conversation.

ambition.what: Weekly triage of emerging stakeholder concerns.

tasks.altitude: Preparation becomes shorter and more consistent, allowing a weekly concern discussion between larger reviews. The specialist gains a stronger evidence base; managers retain business decision authority.

reach.task: Test whether a prominent concern extends beyond vocal stakeholders.
reach.learn: Sampling limits, survey design and the difference between mentions and prevalence.

evidence.claim: Coosto supports conversation and news-topic monitoring; this supports evidence gathering, not automated business advice.
Deterministic collection and reviewed theme classification are feasible; their value depends on source coverage and managerial use.

assumptions: Most discussion and advice remain human, consistent with the communication-heavy prior.
Coverage sources are licensed or otherwise authorised for the intended processing.
The concern brief describes observed evidence rather than measuring population opinion.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; access and any employee consultation follow applicable national rules.
Build ranges cover a pilot and active consultation work, excluding uncertain waiting periods.
unknowns: Which monitoring sources and business updates are available.
Whether concern records can be linked without exposing unnecessary personal data.
Who owns business decisions and can schedule follow-up reviews.
How often managers currently receive usable concern briefings.
research_questions: Which themes require direct stakeholder research before advice is credible?
What evidence would cause managers to reconsider a recorded decision?
new_work: Review theme framing, source selection and contradictory evidence.
Maintain source connectors and topic definitions.
Check whether scheduled decision reviews occur and capture what changed.

tasks.short: Coach representatives to communicate clearly and credibly with the public or employees.

steps.what: Discuss the representative's audience, upcoming communication and development needs.
Prepare practice questions, message examples and a coaching agenda.

loop.input: Coaching brief, approved messages and communication guidelines.
loop.output: Audience-specific questions, hypothetical challenges and source-linked message examples.
loop.check: Check every factual statement against approved material; label hypothetical questions; specialist checks tone and difficulty.
loop.stop: Generate one pack with one revision; unsupported topics return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but realistic questions and examples depend on the audience and situation.

steps.what: Run practice conversations and give specific feedback on delivery and judgement.
Write a personalised practice plan from agreed feedback.

loop.input: Coach-selected notes, agreed goals and approved practice material.
loop.output: Short practice plan with exercises linked to agreed goals.
loop.check: Use only recorded feedback; exclude inferred personality or readiness scores; coach reviews before sharing.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; disputed feedback is resolved by the coach and representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning individual feedback into useful exercises requires limited language generation.

steps.what: Arrange the next practice session and send agreed reminders.

tasks.design: Use approved material in the {DOCS} to generate reviewed practice packs and personalised exercises through bounded drafting loops. The coach runs the sessions and agrees development goals, while the {CALENDAR} and {EMAIL} handle scheduling and agreed reminders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coaching itself depends on trust and observation; tailoring preparation and follow-up previously required repeated manual writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-constrained drafting can produce editable practice material, with existing scheduling features handling routine coordination.
tasks.still_hard: A coach must assess anxiety, credibility and situational judgement. Confidential coaching notes require restricted access and careful retention.
tasks.human_edge: Create psychological safety, give candid feedback and recognise when rehearsed language undermines credibility.
tasks.altitude: The coach spends less time writing packs and can support additional novice speakers. Decisions about coaching goals and readiness remain human and within the existing mandate.

reach.task: Prepare a representative for a difficult public interview.
reach.learn: Escalation boundaries, difficult-question practice and evidence-based readiness discussions.

evidence.claim: A trial involving 444 professionals found faster and higher-rated writing with ChatGPT; it did not establish better coaching outcomes.
Acrolinx supports repeatable checks against a style guide, useful for checking practice material.
Personalised practice packs can support human coaching, but readiness and behavioural feedback require contextual judgement.

assumptions: Live coaching remains the largest time component, consistent with the task priors.
The pilot uses coach-selected notes rather than automatic recordings or employee scoring.
Representatives receive only reviewed practice material.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; employee consultation and coaching-data use follow applicable national rules.
Build ranges include access and consultation effort; formal consultation can extend calendar time.
unknowns: Whether representatives are employees, external clients or both.
Who may access coaching notes and how long they are retained.
Which messages and communication guidelines are approved.
Whether first-time supervisors currently receive communication coaching.
research_questions: Which practice questions do coaches find realistic and useful?
Does reduced preparation time allow additional coaching sessions without reducing quality?
new_work: Review generated scenarios for factual accuracy, tone and difficulty.
Maintain approved message material and coaching templates.
Review access and retention of personal coaching notes.

tasks.short: Study organisational goals and stakeholder needs to develop a public relations strategy.

steps.what: Collect organisational goals, policies, previous results and stakeholder evidence.
Clarify priorities, constraints and stakeholder needs with responsible managers.
Draft strategy options with audiences, messages, channels, assumptions and measures.

loop.input: Approved strategy brief, constraints and source-linked evidence bundle.
loop.output: Up to three strategy options with explicit assumptions, evidence gaps and proposed measures.
loop.check: Trace factual claims to sources; validate budgets and dates deterministically; specialist checks feasibility and framing.
loop.stop: Three options maximum and one revision pass; missing evidence becomes an open question.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates structure the document, but connecting audience needs, messages and alternatives requires contextual drafting.

steps.what: Choose a recommended strategy and resolve conflicting objectives.
Approve the strategy, resource envelope and escalation boundaries.
Transfer approved milestones, owners and measures into the delivery plan.

tasks.design: A deterministic job assembles authorised objectives, results and stakeholder evidence from the {DOCS}, {BI}, {CRM} and {SOCIAL}. A bounded drafting loop fills structured strategy options, while people choose and approve the direction; approved fields populate the {PROJECT} delivery plan and review schedule.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence assembly and document preparation were fragmented, while strategic choices could not be reduced to fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes modest integrations cheaper to build, and source-constrained drafting can accelerate option preparation without assuming better strategic judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Public opinion is uncertain, attribution is weak and organisational objectives may conflict. A polished option can still rest on a poor assumption.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a credible position, understand stakeholder legitimacy and accept responsibility for strategic trade-offs.

ambition.what: Monthly review of the strategy's highest-risk audience assumption.

tasks.altitude: The specialist shifts time from assembling documents to testing assumptions and defending choices. The specialist can propose more frequent adjustments; the manager retains strategy and resource approval.

reach.task: Align public relations objectives with campaign investment decisions.
reach.learn: Budget trade-offs, outcome measures and the limits of attributing business results to communication.

reach.task: Design a small study to test an audience assumption.
reach.learn: Research questions, sampling and useful evidence thresholds.

evidence.claim: The trial of 444 professionals supports faster preparation of writing tasks, not proof of better public relations strategy.
Coosto supports topic monitoring, providing one possible input to strategy evidence gathering.
Full Fact AI flags checkable claims and matches repeats; claim checks do not establish strategic suitability.
Structured approval fields can populate delivery plans deterministically after approval.

assumptions: This is ordinary organisational public relations, without electoral persuasion.
The high amplification prior supports faster preparation; it does not justify automating strategy selection.
Approved strategy fields contain explicit owners, dates and measures before transfer.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; consultation and employee-data requirements follow applicable national rules.
Build ranges assume a limited pilot using supported interfaces and include active access and consultation work.
unknowns: Whether objectives and promotional policies are current and accessible.
Which outcomes have usable baselines and which are only activity counts.
Who can approve resources and strategy changes.
Whether stakeholder evidence is representative enough for the proposed choices.
Which interfaces and internal approvals are available.
research_questions: Which recurring assumption has the greatest effect on strategy choices?
Can option quality be assessed without rewarding document polish over evidence?
Which delivery-plan fields can existing workflow configuration populate reliably?
new_work: Review option evidence, assumptions and factual claims.
Maintain approved strategy templates and field mappings.
Investigate evidence gaps before committing resources.
Review strategy assumptions against subsequent results.

role.altitude: The role keeps its human centre: listening, coaching, advising and choosing credible positions. Preparation and administration shrink, creating room for broader stakeholder contact and more frequent testing of communication assumptions; business and resource authority remain with the designated managers.
reach: Help market research analysts turn stakeholder concerns into answerable research questions.
Help marketing managers connect communication choices to investment and outcome measures.
Help meeting and event planners create accessible listening formats.
skills_to_grow: Source checking and distinguishing evidence from interpretation.
Privacy-aware handling of stakeholder and coaching notes.
Testing bounded drafting outputs and resolving exceptions.
role.ambitious_version: A stakeholder insight and communication advisory service that reaches overlooked groups, supports novice representatives and brings tested audience assumptions into regular management decisions.
